model.rationale: The district's 18-point Republican lean, Messmer's incumbency and clear money advantage, and market pricing near 95 percent Republican all point the same way, and no polling or ratings suggest competitiveness. The forecast stays with a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or any polling showing Messmer well below typical incumbent margins would be the first sign of a real contest, but nothing of the kind is visible now.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 8th District sits in the state's strongly Republican southwest, with a partisan lean of about 18 points toward the GOP. Mark Messmer, the Republican incumbent, runs for re-election with the built-in advantages of incumbency in territory that has consistently elected Republicans. Democrat Mary Allen, a first-time challenger, faces a steep structural deficit.

Messmer has raised about $1.4 million and holds a five-to-one cash advantage over Allen, who has brought in roughly $493,000. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters currently list the race as competitive. Prediction markets price Messmer's chances at roughly 95 percent. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican win, with the remaining uncertainty mostly about the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
